Q: Error starting FreeIPA server as docker container A:

I also faced this same issue and tried many things but sadly docker is not compatible with FreeIPA. Instead I used podman for the containerization and it worked perfectly. Though there has to be some configuration to be done before setting it up.

This is the full guide on how I set it up .

https://dev.to/chanuth_412/running-freeipa-on-ubuntu-using-podman-part-2-step-by-step-deployment-3ngc

Q: How to compile this Java Server/Client code in CMD A:

you can choose a directory for your root home like D:/. then

  1. make a new folder named program (it's your package name)

  2. put the Server.java and Client.java into program

  3. open the CMD and cd to root path

  4. execute: javac program/Server.java (maybe program\Server.java on windows)

  5. execute: java program.Server

  6. it's run!

Q: Mongo delete and insert vs update A:

I think the easiest way is to redo the statistics if you were doing it in mongo (e.g. using the aggregation framework). If you index upsers documents properly it should be fine. I assume that your statistics update is an offline operation.

Q: Arithmetic overflow error converting float to data type numeric with positive exponents but not negative exponents A:

Based on your tests in 1) and 2), it looks like you're trying to find the upper bounds for int and float and lower bounds for float using the numeric(38,19) data type. The int bounds will be determined by the scale factor (19), and the precision bounds are defined for the numeric data type (see below).

Maximum precision in SQL Server is -10^38 +1 through 10^38 –1 according to MSDN. Minimum precision will round based on the value for NUMERIC_ROUNDABORT.

If this is a scientific application, you may want to read the MSDN description of precision, length, and scale, especially if you are performing operations with the values stored in the numeric column.

Q: Golang auto referencing, not always possible to get the address of a value A:

I just explored that. Here age(20).print() gives us an error because the print() method expected a variable address. Suppose we give an age(20).print(), that will not be accepted because of its value, like &12 working like that. We need to send a variable with the address myAge: = age (20); it's a value of age type. We need to send the variable address (&myAge).print(). But GoLang has auto-dereferencing, which is why it internally works like (&myAge).
